title: PageIndex builds a document tree for reasoning-based RAG
friendlyTitle: PageIndex helps AI navigate long documents by structure
summary: PageIndex is an MIT-licensed document indexing project for vectorless, reasoning-based retrieval. It builds a hierarchical representation that lets an LLM navigate long professional documents using structure and context rather than relying only on chunk similarity.
friendlySummary: PageIndex turns a document into a tree that an AI can follow. It is an alternative to finding text only by matching similar chunks.
whyItMatters: Use it to prototype retrieval over reports, manuals and other structured documents where headings and relationships matter. Its cookbooks and examples offer a practical starting point for comparing tree-guided retrieval with an existing vector RAG pipeline.
friendlyWhyItMatters: Try it with reports or manuals where sections and headings matter. Compare its answers with your current search or RAG system before changing production.
